components.name: Button
components.summary: Starts an action on the current page, such as saving, exporting or opening a menu.

whenToUse.t: To start an action on the current page: New listing, Export, Save view.
To open a menu or popover of more actions, with a chevron on the right.
For the one step most people take next in a view, using the primary style.
As an icon-only ghost button for frequent, well-known row actions where space is tight.

whenNotToUse.t: To go to another page or URL. Use a link (button-link style) instead.
To switch between views of the same data. Use the Segmented control.
To turn a setting on or off. Use a Switch, not a button whose label flips.
For a long set of secondary actions on one object. Group them in a Dropdown menu.

guidelines.t: Seven variants, using shadcn names: default (the primary), outline (white with a light border), secondary (grey fill), ghost (no fill until hover), warning (risky but reversible, a TwoUX addition), destructive (red, inside a confirmation) and link. Pick by importance in the view, not by looks.
Only one primary button per view. In a dialog or side panel with its own task, that container may have its own primary.
Four sizes: 24px inside rows, 28px in toolbars and filter bars, 32px by default, 36px only for the single action of an empty state or sign-in page. Icon-only buttons are square at the same height.
States: default, hover, focus (2px primary ring with a 2px white gap), pressed, disabled (45% opacity), loading.
Avoid disabled buttons in forms. Keep Publish pressable and show what is missing through validation.
When a button must be disabled, give the reason in a tooltip or nearby text.
While an action runs, use loading: the spinner replaces the leading icon, the button ignores clicks and stays focusable, so it cannot be pressed twice and keyboard users keep their place.

content.t: Start with a verb and say what happens: Publish listing, Export 2 rows, Close listings.
Sentence case, no full stop, no articles: Save view, not Save The View.
Two to four words. Add the object for destructive actions: Delete listing, not Delete.
Add an ellipsis when the action needs more input before it runs: Extend to a date…
Never OK or Yes in a dialog. Name both outcomes: Close listings and Keep open.

accessibility.t: Use a native button element. Enter and Space activate it.
Icon-only buttons need an aria-label naming the action, plus a tooltip showing the same words.
The accessible name must contain the visible label so voice users can say what they see.
Focus ring and secondary border need at least 3:1 against the background; label text at least 4.5:1, white on primary included.
The 28px small button meets the 24px minimum target. Do not shrink icon buttons below 24px.
Menu buttons set aria-haspopup and aria-expanded.

keyboard.action: Activate the focused button
Run the action from anywhere in the view

components.name: Split button
components.summary: A button joined to a chevron: the button runs the usual action (Import data), the chevron opens its variants (Import all, Import selection).
structure: Chevron part with its own name, opening a menu

whenToUse.t: One action is the usual choice and a few close variants of it are needed now and then, such as Import data with Import all and Import selection.
Space is tight and the variants belong together, as in a table header toolbar.

whenNotToUse.t: For unrelated actions. Use separate buttons, or a Dropdown menu behind More actions.
When no option is clearly the usual one. Use a menu button (Button with a chevron) so people choose every time.
For a destructive main action. Put destructive variants in the menu, never on the main part.

guidelines.t: Use SplitButton instead of joining a Button and a menu by hand, so the parts, divider, names and menu alignment are the same everywhere.
The main part runs the action at once; the chevron only opens the menu. Repeat the main action first in the menu so the list is complete.
Outline by default. Use the primary variant only when it is the view's one primary action.
Disable a variant that can't run yet (Import selection with nothing selected) rather than hiding it, and say why nearby.

content.t: Main label: a verb and an object, Import data. Menu items: short variants, Import all, Import selection.
Name the chevron by what it opens: More import options.

accessibility.t: Two buttons in a group: the main button, then a menu button with aria-haspopup, aria-expanded and its own accessible name.
2.5.8 Target size: the chevron part is at least 24px wide.

keyboard.action: Move from the main part to the chevron
Run the main action, or open the menu from the chevron
Open the menu on the first item
Close the menu and return to the chevron

components.name: Text input
components.summary: Lets people type a single line of text, such as a job title, a salary or a search term.

whenToUse.t: For short free text that cannot be listed in advance: job title, salary, a reference number. For dates use the Date picker (date-picker).
For search inside a view, with a search icon and an accessible label.
With a prefix or suffix for units the person should not type: £ and per year.

whenNotToUse.t: To pick one option from a short known list. Use Radio buttons (up to seven) or a select.
For a yes/no setting. Use a Checkbox or Switch.
For choosing from existing categories. Use Combobox (combobox) so people choose instead of type; for several free values use Tag input (tag-input).

guidelines.t: 32px high, 6px radius, 13px text. Label sits above the field, left-aligned, 6px gap.
Hint text sits under the field and stays visible while typing. Use it for format and examples.
No placeholder in place of a label. Use placeholders only for a short example, or not at all.
Focus shows an primary border and a soft 3px ring. Invalid shows a red border plus a text message under the field.
Check the value when the person leaves the field, not while they type. Clear the error as soon as the value is fixed.
Accept common variations (18000, 18,000, £18k) and convert them, then show the cleaned value.

content.t: Labels are short nouns in sentence case without a colon: Job title, Salary, Closing date.
Hint text says why or in what format: Shown on the listing and in search results.
Mark required fields with an asterisk after the label.
Error text uses UK English and says how to fix it: Enter at least £23,400.

accessibility.t: Every field has a visible label tied to it with for/id. A placeholder is not a label.
Link hint and error to the field with aria-describedby; set aria-invalid="true" when it fails.
Field border needs 3:1 against the surface; typed text and hint text 4.5:1.
The asterisk is decorative (aria-hidden). Use the required attribute so screen readers announce it.
Error is not shown by colour alone: red border plus written message.

keyboard.action: Move into and out of the field
Focus the search field of the current view (single-key shortcut, can be turned off)
Leave the search field

components.name: Date picker
components.summary: Enter a calendar date, or a range of dates, by typing it or choosing it on a calendar: a closing date, a start date, a reporting period.
structure: Field: the date as dd/mm/yyyy (From and To for a range)
Popover: preset periods (range, optional), month heading, previous and next month, grid starting on Monday
Footer: why some dates are unavailable (optional)
Hint or error under the field

whenToUse.t: For a date people set on a record: closing date, start date, contract end.
For a period that narrows a list or a chart: applications in the last 30 days, a quarter for a report.
When people need to see the weekday or the week around a date, such as booking around weekends.

whenNotToUse.t: For a date people know by heart and never browse to, such as a date of birth. Use a Text input (text-input) with the hint dd/mm/yyyy.
For booking or moving events in time. Use the Scheduler (scheduler).
For a chart's fixed period options such as Daily or Weekly. Use a Segmented control (segmented-control).
To show a date. Use Timestamp (timestamp).

guidelines.t: Typing is the main path: the field accepts 12/03/2026, 12/3/26, 12 Mar 2026 and 2026-03-12, and rewrites the value as 12/03/2026 when people leave it, so they see how it was read.
The calendar is the second path: the button at the end of the field, or Alt+↓ in the field. It opens on the value's month, otherwise today's.
Values are ISO calendar dates ("2026-03-12"), never a Date at midnight UTC, so they match Timestamp and don't land on the day before west of London.
Weeks start on Monday and month and weekday names are UK English.
Say why dates are unavailable in the footer, such as "Closing dates must be on a weekday." Unavailable days are skipped by the arrow keys.
A range shows two months side by side from 768px, one below. The first pick sets the start, the second the end; days between are filled as people point or move.

Preset periods (Last 7 days, Last 30 days, This month…) apply at once. In a filter they are stored by name, so a saved view still means "last 30 days" next month. In a filter bar use DateFilterPill, which reads as a sentence like other filter pills: Applied is in Last 30 days.
Check the value when people leave the field and on submit; show the error under the field, never in a toast.

content.t: The hint is the format: dd/mm/yyyy. Add a reason only when it helps: "The last day applications are accepted."
Errors say what to do: "Enter the closing date as dd/mm/yyyy, such as 12/03/2026.", "Choose a date on or after 7 December 2026.", "The end date is before the start date. Change one of them."
Preset names say the period: Last 7 days, This month, Last quarter.

accessibility.t: The popover is a dialog named "Choose date". The grid's day buttons have full names: "Thursday 12 March 2026", with "Today" and "selected" added.
The month heading is a polite live region, so changing month is read out.
Focus moves to the selected day, or today, when the calendar opens, and back to the field when it closes.
Today has a ring and the selected day a fill, and both are named, so neither relies on colour alone.
Day cells are 32px, above the 24px minimum target.

keyboard.action: Open the calendar from the field
Read the typed date
Previous or next day; same day in the previous or next week
Start or end of the week
Previous or next month (Shift for the year)
Choose the focused day
Close the calendar without changing the value; focus returns to the field

components.name: Combobox
components.summary: Pick one or several values from a long list by typing a few letters, and add a missing one without leaving the form: a location, skills, an owner.
structure: Trigger: the value, or chosen values as tags then +N more
Options, grouped (optional), with a check for chosen ones and secondary text
Status: searching, no match, or failed with Try again
Footer for several: count, limit and Clear

whenToUse.t: One value from eight or more options, such as a location from 40 offices.
Several values from eight or more options, such as skills from a long list (multiple).
Options the server searches, such as people in a large company (filter={null} with onSearch).
When a missing option can be created on the spot: Create "Leeds office".

whenNotToUse.t: Up to seven options. Show them all as Radio buttons (radio) or Checkboxes (checkbox).
Free values with no list, such as email addresses. Use Tag input (tag-input).
Narrowing a list or a table. Use Filter pills (filter-bar).
Running commands or jumping anywhere. Use the Command palette (command-palette).

guidelines.t: Matching ignores case and accents and looks at the label and the secondary text.
With several values, chosen options are listed first when the list opens and keep their place while people tick, so rows don't jump.
For server search, results replace the list in one go. "Searching…" shows only if the wait passes one second.
If options fail to load, say so inside the list with Try again; the rest of the form keeps working.
Offer Create only when nothing matches exactly. A name-only record is created and selected at once; anything more opens an overlay side panel and is selected when saved.
Up to three chosen values show as tags in the trigger, then +N more. The footer states the count and any limit.
A required combobox shows its error under the field on submit; the submit button is never disabled.

content.t: The placeholder names the action and the thing: Choose a location. The search field says Search locations.
No match names the text: No locations match "lee".
Create repeats the text in quotes: Create "Leeds office".

accessibility.t: The search field is a combobox controlling a listbox; options are named and the highlighted one is announced with aria-activedescendant.
The trigger is named by the label and the value: "Location, Leeds" or "Skills, 3 selected".
Result counts and the searching state are announced politely.
Each tag's remove button is named "Remove Python" and has a 24px target.

keyboard.action: Open the list
Open the list with that letter in the search
Move through options
Choose the option; with several values it ticks and the list stays open
Close without changing the value; focus returns to the trigger
Move to the last chosen tag; Backspace again removes it

components.name: Tag input
components.summary: Enter several short values that don't come from a list, typed or pasted, and see at once which are wrong: email addresses to invite, allowed domains, keywords.
structure: Field holding the tags, then the text input
Tag: text and remove button; an invalid tag adds an alert icon and its reason
Hint, or what just happened (added, already added, not added)
Count when there is a limit: 3 of 10

whenToUse.t: For free values with no list to pick from: invite emails, allowed domains, search keywords.
When people paste a list from a spreadsheet, an email client or another tool.

whenNotToUse.t: When the values come from a list, such as skills or locations. Use Combobox (combobox) with multiple.
For one value. Use a Text input (text-input).
For labels on a record that people only read. Use Tag (tag).
For many rows of values with several fields each. Use a Sheet grid (sheet-grid).

guidelines.t: Enter, comma or leaving the field adds the typed text. Tab adds it only when there is text, so the field never traps focus.
Pasted text is split on commas, semicolons, new lines and tabs, so a column from Excel or a list from Outlook works.
A duplicate (ignoring case) isn't added again: the existing tag is highlighted and the hint line says it is already added.
An invalid value stays as a marked tag with its reason; the error under the field counts them. Nothing is dropped without saying so.
Values past the limit stay in the input, and the hint line says how many weren't added.
Fix a value by pressing Enter on its tag, or double-clicking it: the text goes back into the input.

content.t: The hint names the separators and the thing: Separate addresses with commas or new lines.
Messages say what happened and what to do: "anna@acme.co.uk is already added.", "Not an email address.", "2 addresses aren't valid. Fix or remove them."

accessibility.t: The tags are a list named by the field label. Each tag's name includes its reason when it isn't valid.
Adding, removing and paste summaries ("12 added, 2 not valid") are announced politely.
The field is one tab stop; arrow keys move between tags, so long lists don't flood the tab order.
Error is shown with an icon and words as well as colour.

keyboard.action: Add the typed text

keyboard.keys: ← or Backspace at the start of the input
keyboard.action: Move to the last tag
Move between tags; → from the last tag returns to the input
Remove it; focus moves to the tag before or after
Put its text back in the input to fix it
Return to the input

components.name: Form validation
components.summary: Tells people which fields need fixing and how, at the field and in a summary at the top on submit.

whenToUse.t: On any form where a value can be wrong or missing: a new listing, a salary, a closing date.
Field errors as soon as the person leaves a field with a wrong value.
The summary strip when someone submits and one or more fields fail.

whenNotToUse.t: For errors not tied to a field, such as a server failure. Use a banner above the form or the table error state.
To confirm success on every field. Use a Toast for the completed action instead.
Before the person has touched the field. Leave untouched fields neutral until submit.

guidelines.t: Check a field when the person leaves it. Recheck on each keystroke once it is in error, and clear the error when fixed.
On submit, check the whole form. Show the red strip at the top: 2 fields need fixing before you can publish.
The strip has a Go to first link that scrolls to and focuses the first field in error.
The summary adds to inline errors; it never replaces them.
Message sits directly under the field, replacing the hint, in 12px red text.
Keep everything the person typed. Never clear a form on error.

content.t: Say what to do, not what went wrong in system terms: Pick a date after today.
For empty fields, instruct: Enter a job title. For wrong values, describe the limit: Enter at least £23,400.
No please, sorry, oops, invalid or blaming words.
Use the field label in the message so it reads as one thing, and use the same words in the summary.
The summary counts problems in plain words: 2 fields need fixing before you can publish.

accessibility.t: Each failed field has aria-invalid="true" and aria-describedby pointing at its message.
Errors are in text, not only red. The border colour is a second cue.
The strip uses role="alert" so it is announced at once; Go to first moves focus to the field.
Messages suggest a fix whenever the system knows one.
Red text and the red border meet 4.5:1 and 3:1 on white.

keyboard.action: Leave a field and trigger its check
Move focus to the first field in error

components.name: Checkbox
components.summary: Lets people choose any number of options, or confirm one setting that is applied when they save.

whenToUse.t: To pick any number of options from a list, including none.
To select table rows for bulk actions, with a header checkbox that selects all.
For a single setting in a form that is applied when the person saves: Show salary on listing.
As a parent with an indeterminate dash when only some children are selected.

whenNotToUse.t: For one choice out of several. Use Radio.
For a setting that takes effect at once. Use Switch.
To switch the view of other content. Use Segmented control.

guidelines.t: Box is 15px, 4px radius. Checked and indeterminate fill with primary.
The label is part of the click target. Clicking either toggles the box.
List options vertically, one per line. Horizontal only for two short options with clear spacing.
Indeterminate is visual only; clicking it selects all rows.
Opt-in checkboxes start unticked.

content.t: Write labels positively: Accept CVs by email, not Don't accept CVs by email.
Keep labels short, sentence case, no end punctuation.
Group labels say what to choose: Columns to show.

accessibility.t: Use a native input type="checkbox" with a label element. Space toggles it.
Parent checkboxes expose aria-checked="mixed" when partly selected.
Wrap related checkboxes in a fieldset with a legend, or role="group" with aria-labelledby.
The 15px box is below 24px, so the label is clickable and rows are 36px apart to meet target spacing.
Unchecked border and checked fill need 3:1 against white.

keyboard.action: Toggle the focused checkbox
Select the focused table row (single-key shortcut, can be turned off)
Extend row selection down or up

components.name: Radio
components.summary: Lets people choose exactly one option from a short, visible list in a form.

whenToUse.t: To pick one option from two to seven, when seeing all options helps the decision: Full time or Part time.
When both choices need a visible explanation, which a single checkbox cannot give.
Inside a form that is applied with a Save or Publish button.

whenNotToUse.t: For eight or more options. Use a select or Dropdown menu.
For several choices at once. Use Checkbox.
To switch the view of data outside a form. Use Segmented control.
For a single on/off setting. Use Checkbox or Switch.

guidelines.t: Circle is 15px; selected shows a thick primary ring.
Preselect the most likely or safest option. Never preselect a risky one.
Add None when no choice is valid, since a radio group cannot be cleared.
Stack options vertically. Inline is allowed for two short options, as in Full time / Part time.
Order from most to least likely, or least to most risky.

content.t: Labels short and parallel, ideally under three words.
The legend asks or names the choice: Contract type.
Avoid overlapping ranges in number options.

accessibility.t: Native radios share a name, wrapped in fieldset and legend (or role="radiogroup" with a label).
Tab enters the group on the selected option; arrow keys move and select.
Labels are clickable so the target exceeds the 15px circle.
Ring and border have 3:1 contrast against white.

keyboard.action: Move into the group, onto the selected option
Move to and select the next or previous option
Select the focused option if not selected

components.name: Switch
components.summary: Turns one setting on or off with immediate effect, without a Save button.

whenToUse.t: For a setting that applies the moment it is flipped: Email me when someone applies.
For preferences in popovers and panels: Wrap long text, Single-key shortcuts.
When the label describes the on state clearly enough on its own.

whenNotToUse.t: In a form that needs Save or Publish. Use Checkbox.
When both states need explaining, such as cost differences. Use Radio.
For more than two options. Use Radio or Segmented control.

guidelines.t: Track 28 x 16px, thumb 12px. On fills primary; off is grey.
The change applies at once. Confirm it with a short toast when the effect is not visible on screen.
Label to the left in settings rows, right of the switch in inline lists; keep one pattern per surface.
If disabled, say why nearby.
Movement of the thumb is the main cue; colour is the second.

content.t: Label says what is on when the switch is on. Read it with on/off after it to test.
The label never changes with the state.
Lead with the key word, no question: Single-key shortcuts, not Do you want single-key shortcuts?

accessibility.t: Use role="switch" (or a native checkbox) with aria-checked true/false.
Space toggles; Enter may also toggle.
Label tied with for/id so the label row is part of the target; the 28 x 16 track alone is under 24px high.
Off track and on fill need 3:1 against the surface.
Changing a switch must not move focus or open a new view.

keyboard.action: Toggle the focused switch
Also toggles (optional)

components.name: Status badge
components.summary: Shows the system state of a record, such as Live, Draft or Closed early, in one short word or phrase.

whenToUse.t: To show workflow or system state of a listing or candidate: Live, Expires in 3 days, Closed early, Draft.
In table rows, where a word reads faster than an icon alone.
Next to the object it describes, never floating on its own.

whenNotToUse.t: For user-made categories such as Design or Graduate scheme. Use Tag.
To start an action or change state. Use a Dropdown menu or Button; the badge is static.
For counts on tabs or filters. Use a plain count next to the label.

guidelines.t: 20px high, 4px radius, 12px medium text, 1px border in the tone colour on a tinted background.
Five tones with fixed meaning: ok (green), warn (amber), bad (red), mute (grey), accent (primary, for Featured).
Match the tone to the meaning, not to how much attention you want.
Keep the same tone for the same status everywhere in the product.
Do not truncate. If the text is long, rewrite it; badges cannot be focused to reveal the rest.

content.t: One to three words, sentence case: Expires in 3 days, not EXPIRING SOON.
Use plain words people use, not system codes.
Prefer a specific state over a vague one: Closed early, not Inactive.

accessibility.t: The text carries the meaning; colour only reinforces it.
Text on the tinted background needs 4.5:1; the border 3:1 is not required because the text identifies it.
Badges are not interactive: no tabindex, no tooltip that holds needed information.
When a status changes live (for example after an agent run), announce it with a status message.

components.name: Tag
components.summary: Labels a record with a category people chose, such as Design, Hybrid or Graduate scheme.

whenToUse.t: For descriptive categories that classify or group records: team, contract type, work mode.
For user-defined values that people add and remove.
When one record belongs to several categories.

whenNotToUse.t: For system state such as Live or Closed. Use Status badge.
As a button. Use Button or a selectable control.

guidelines.t: 22px high, 4px corners, white with a 1px grey border, 12px text, so it reads quieter than a status badge. Not fully round: in TwoUX a pill means a filter you can remove.
Add a colour dot only when the colour means something, such as the team.
Removable tags put a small x after the text.
Show up to three in a table cell; summarise the rest as +N so the row stays scannable.
Never wrap a tag over two lines. Truncate with a tooltip showing the full text.

content.t: One or two words, ideally under 20 characters.
Sentence case unless a proper noun: Graduate scheme, not Graduate Scheme.
Use the same wording everywhere so filters match.

accessibility.t: Text contrast 4.5:1 on white; the dot is decorative and hidden from assistive technology.
The remove button is a real button named Remove Design.
Remove buttons need a 24px target or enough spacing from neighbours.
Colour never carries the only meaning; the text names the category.

keyboard.action: Move to a removable tag's remove button
Remove the tag

components.name: Tabs (underline)
components.summary: Splits one record or page into sections such as Overview, Candidates and Activity, one visible at a time.

whenToUse.t: To split a record into separate sections people do not need side by side: Overview, Candidates, Activity.
When each section is substantial and can have its own URL.
With a count when the number helps people decide to open the tab: Candidates 42.

whenNotToUse.t: To switch between views of the same data, such as All / Active. Use Segmented control.
For steps in a flow. Use a stepper or separate pages.
When people must compare content across sections. Show it on one page.
For app navigation. Use the sidebar.

guidelines.t: Single row, 20px gap, 13px medium labels. Active tab gets primary text and a 2px primary underline: two cues, not one.
Two to seven tabs. Order by use, most used first; the first tab is the default.
No nested tabs and no disabled tabs; hide a tab that does not apply.
If tabs overflow on narrow screens, the list scrolls sideways; it never wraps to a second row.
Put shared headings and actions above the tab list, not inside one panel.

content.t: One or two words, nouns, sentence case: Activity, not View all activity.
Labels must not overlap in meaning.
Counts need screen reader text: 42 candidates, not just 42.

accessibility.t: role="tablist" with a label, role="tab" with aria-selected and aria-controls, role="tabpanel" labelled by its tab.
Tab enters the list on the active tab; Left and Right arrows move between tabs; Home and End jump.
Panels load instantly, so tabs activate on focus (automatic activation).
The underline indicator has 3:1 against white.
Tab hit area is the full label height (about 36px), above the 24px minimum.

keyboard.action: Previous or next tab
First or last tab
Move from the tab list into the panel

components.name: Segmented control
components.summary: Switches between two or three views or settings of the same content, such as All, Active and Backlog.

whenToUse.t: To switch how the same data is shown or filtered: All / Active / Backlog, Chart / Table.
For a view setting that always has a value: Rows per page 25 / 50 / 100, Daily / Weekly.
When there are two or three short options and room to show them.

whenNotToUse.t: For separate sections of a record. Use Tabs.
For more than three options. Use a Dropdown menu or select.
For an on/off setting. Use Switch.
For choices inside a form that is saved later. Use Radio.

guidelines.t: Track is grey with a 2px inset; segments are 24px high, 12px medium text; selected segment is white with a hairline shadow.
The change applies immediately, like a switch.
Equal weight for all segments; one is always selected.
Deactivate at most one segment, and give the reason in a tooltip.

content.t: One word per segment where possible.
Sentence case, parallel words: All, Active, Backlog.
Icon-only segments need alternative text naming the view.

accessibility.t: TwoUX renders it as a group of toggle buttons: role="group" with aria-label, each button with aria-pressed.
Every segment label stays the same when pressed; state comes from aria-pressed.
Segments are 24px high, exactly the WCAG 2.5.8 minimum; do not make them smaller.
The selected segment differs by fill and shadow, with 3:1 against the track.
Visible focus ring on each segment.

keyboard.action: Move to each segment
Select the focused segment

components.name: Dropdown menu
components.summary: Opens a short list of actions or options from a button, with optional groups and one level of submenus.
structure: Menu item: icon, label, shortcut or current value

whenToUse.t: To group related actions behind one button: Export, row actions, Add context.
For about 5 to 15 commands, ordered by how often they are used.
For settings with a current value, shown on the right and changed in a one-level submenu: Writing style Concise.

whenNotToUse.t: For one or two actions. Show them as Buttons.
When people must search or pick from a long list of values. Use a select or combobox.
For the main action in a view. Use a primary Button.
For rich content or forms. Use a popover or dialog.

guidelines.t: Panel 200px minimum, 10px radius, 4px padding, shadow. Items 30px high, 6px radius, hover in grey.
Group with uppercase group labels and separators; put destructive items last, in red, after a separator.
At most one level of submenu. Submenus open on hover, focus or Right arrow, and flip to the side with room.

Icons on items: none by default. Add them only when every item in a group has a well-known icon from the icon meaning table, and then on all items in that group; never on one item alone. The label always stays, and the icon is 14px and muted.
Show each item's shortcut on the right.
Disable items that do not apply rather than hide them, so people can still find them.
Keep the list under about 12 items.

content.t: Action items start with a verb; navigation items are nouns.
Sentence case, one line, no articles: Duplicate listing.
Front-load the key word so the list scans: Export CSV, Export PDF.
Ellipsis for items that open more input: Extend to a date…

accessibility.t: Trigger has aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded. Enter, Space or Down opens and focuses the first item.
role="menu" with menuitem, menuitemcheckbox or menuitemradio; checked items use aria-checked.
Up and Down move, Right opens a submenu, Left closes it, Esc closes and returns focus to the trigger.
Items are 30px high, above the 24px target minimum.
Focus returns to the trigger on close, so the person is not lost.

keyboard.action: Open the menu and focus the first item
Move between items
Open a submenu
Close a submenu
First or last item
Jump to the next item starting with it
Close and return focus to the trigger

components.name: Tooltip
components.summary: Shows a short, non-essential label or hint on hover or focus, such as an icon button's name and its shortcut.

whenToUse.t: To name an icon-only button: More, Add to Interviewing.
To show the shortcut for a control: Search listings /.
To show the full text of a truncated value, or the exact date behind a relative date.
To give a short reason why a control is disabled.

whenNotToUse.t: For anything needed to finish the task, such as format rules. Use hint text under the field.
For links, buttons or more than a sentence. Use a popover.
On labelled buttons, repeating the label.
On status badges or other non-interactive elements.

guidelines.t: Dark ink background, white 12px medium text, 5 x 8px padding, 6px radius.
Appears after a short delay (about 500ms) on hover or keyboard focus, so it does not flicker.
Stays while the pointer is over the trigger or the tooltip, until Esc or blur.
Placed so it never covers the thing it describes, and flips to stay on screen.
One line; never truncated.

content.t: A few words, no full stop: Search listings.
For icon buttons, name the action in one or two words.
Use the same words as the accessible name.

accessibility.t: role="tooltip", referenced by the trigger's aria-describedby. Focus stays on the trigger.
Esc dismisses it without moving focus; the pointer can move onto it; it does not time out.
A tooltip does not give an icon button its name; the button also needs aria-label.
Only on focusable triggers, so keyboard users see it too.
Shortcuts in tooltips are hidden from assistive technology; list them in the shortcut sheet as well.

keyboard.action: Show the tooltip
Hide the tooltip

components.name: Keyboard shortcut hint
components.summary: Prints the key or keys that run an action, on its button, menu item or tooltip, so people learn shortcuts by using the product.
structure: Further key caps for chords or sequences

whenToUse.t: On buttons and menu items whose action has a shortcut: Try again R, Edit E.
In tooltips of icon-only buttons.
In the command palette, the ? shortcut sheet and footers that list navigation keys.

whenNotToUse.t: For shortcuts that do not work in the current context. Leave the hint out.
As the only way to reach an action. Every shortcut duplicates a visible control.
Inside body text as decoration. Use plain text such as press Esc.

guidelines.t: Key cap is 18px high, 4px radius, 2px bottom border, grey surface. On buttons it shrinks to 16px and sits after the label.
On primary buttons the cap is translucent white so it keeps contrast on primary.
Chords show keys side by side (⌘ K); sequences show them in order (G then L).
Render ⌘ on Mac and Ctrl elsewhere.
Reserve shortcuts for frequent actions; keep them to one or two keys and never override copy, paste or undo.

content.t: Use symbols for modifiers and capitals for letters: ⌘, ⇧, ↵, Esc, E.
Use mnemonic keys: E for Edit, C for Create, F for Filter.
The same action keeps the same key everywhere.

accessibility.t: Single-key shortcuts (J, K, X, E, /) can be turned off in the shortcut sheet; ⌘ shortcuts stay on.
Shortcuts avoid keys used by screen readers, such as Caps Lock and Insert combinations.
The hint is visual. The full list is in the ? sheet so assistive technology users can find it.
Every action also works by Tab and Enter.
Key cap text has at least 4.5:1 contrast on its background.

keyboard.action: Open the command palette
Open the shortcut sheet
Go to listings
Next or previous row
New listing
Edit

components.name: Avatar and avatar stack
components.summary: Shows who owns or is linked to a record, as a photo or initials, and several people as an overlapping stack with +N.
structure: Stack: overlapping avatars with 2px white ring

whenToUse.t: To show the owner of a listing or the recruiter on a candidate, next to their name or in a table cell.
A stack when several people relate to one record and space is short.

whenNotToUse.t: When each person must be clearly identified. List names in full.
For a single person in a stack. Use one avatar.
For teams or categories. Use Tag.

guidelines.t: 22px circle, 10px semibold white initials on a colour assigned per person; photo when one exists.
Stack shows up to three, overlapping by 6px with a 2px white ring, then +N in small grey text.
+N reveals the hidden names on hover or focus.
Each person keeps the same colour everywhere.

content.t: Initials stand in when there is no photo, and are hidden from screen readers when the name is shown.
The +N count says how many people are hidden, not the total.
Tooltips on avatars show the full name, matching the alt text.

accessibility.t: Standalone avatars have alt text with the person's name; next to a visible name they are decorative (empty alt).
A stack has a label (for example Candidates) and screen reader text for +N: 3 more candidates.
White initials need 4.5:1 on the assigned colour; pick colours that pass.
If the avatar opens a tooltip or popover it must be focusable.
Interactive avatars are 22px, so keep 24px spacing from other targets.

keyboard.action: Focus the overflow count and show hidden names

components.name: Popover rules
components.summary: Shared behaviour for every floating layer (menus, filters, snooze, selectors): one open at a time and never cut off.

whenToUse.t: For short supporting content or a small set of controls tied to a trigger: filter values, snooze times, column choices.
When the person must stay in context and the page behind stays usable.

whenNotToUse.t: For long reading or a multi-step task. Use a dialog or side panel.
For a one-line label. Use Tooltip.
Inside another popover. Open a submenu (one level) or a dialog instead.
For required fields that would be lost on outside click. Use a dialog.

guidelines.t: Only one popover is open at a time; opening a menu, filter, snooze or selector closes any other.
Popovers open on a user action, never on page load.
Placement flips and shifts to stay inside the panel and the screen, 8px from the edge. Nothing is ever cut off.
Open 4 to 6px from the trigger, aligned to its start edge.
Close on outside click, Esc, or when focus leaves; return focus to the trigger.
Only the body scrolls, never sideways.

content.t: Header in sentence case, one short line, when the popover can be dismissed.
No help articles or Learn more links inside; keep help at page level.
Footer buttons follow Button wording: Cancel and Apply.

accessibility.t: Triggers set aria-expanded (and aria-haspopup for menus). Enter or Space opens.
Give the panel a role (menu or dialog) and a label.
Esc closes and focus returns to the trigger.
The popover must not hide the focused element.
At 320px width it fits without sideways scrolling.

keyboard.action: Open or close from the trigger
Close and return focus to the trigger
Move through controls inside; leaving closes it

components.name: Sign in
components.summary: Provider buttons first, then email. Single sign-on is found from the email domain, and an email link means no password to remember.
structure: Continue button (becomes "Continue with SSO" for SSO domains)

whenToUse.t: The first screen of an account: sign in and create account in one flow.
Letting people choose how they sign in: a provider, single sign-on or an email link.

whenNotToUse.t: Asking for anything beyond how to sign in. Setup questions belong in Onboarding step (onboarding-step).
Gating content that people could read first. Show it before asking them to sign in.

guidelines.t: Put provider buttons first, then email. One primary action: the email button.
Find single sign-on from the email domain. Say "twoux.example signs in with single sign-on" and change the button to Continue with SSO.
Use an email link so there is no password to remember or retype.
Put errors under the field and say what to do, for example "This email uses Google to sign in. Continue with Google instead."
Do not reveal which part was wrong, or whether an account exists, unless the product already shows that elsewhere. Use the same message either way.
Set autocomplete on every field (email, current-password, one-time-code) so browsers and password managers can fill them.
Validate on press, not on every keystroke, and keep the email people typed after an error.

content.t: Button: "Continue with Google", "Continue with email", "Continue with SSO".
Field error: "Enter your work email, for example sam@company.com."
Do not write "Wrong password" or "No account found". Write what to try next.

accessibility.t: The email field has a visible label and the right type and autocomplete values (SC 1.3.5, 3.3.2).
The error is linked to the field with aria-invalid and the field description, and is announced when it appears (SC 3.3.1, 4.1.3).
Signing in never depends on remembering or transcribing a password alone: providers and email links are alternatives (SC 3.3.8).

keyboard.action: Move through the provider buttons, the email field and the primary button
In the email field, submit the form
Press the focused provider button

components.name: File drop
components.summary: Drop a file or choose one. Accepted types and the size limit show before choosing, and a preview replaces the icon once a file is picked.
structure: Drop area (icon or preview, "Drop a file here", accepted types and limit)
Remove and Replace or Upload buttons

whenToUse.t: A single file the product needs, such as a logo, an avatar or a CSV.
Where dragging a file in is a shortcut, not the only way.

whenNotToUse.t: Attaching files to a message. Use the Message composer (message-composer).
Importing many files with progress. Use a list with a status per file.

guidelines.t: Show accepted types and the size limit before anyone chooses a file.
Let people choose with a button as well as drop. Drag and drop is never the only way.
Errors name the file's size or type and say what to choose, for example "That file is 14.2 MB. Choose one up to 10 MB."
The preview replaces the icon, with Remove and Replace beside it.
Use a visible label, and a native file input that is hidden visually but still labelled and focusable by the Upload button.

content.t: Hint: "PNG or JPEG, up to 10 MB".
Wrong type: "That file type isn't supported. Choose PNG or JPEG."

accessibility.t: The visible label is attached to the real input, which keeps its accessible name and value (SC 3.3.2, 4.1.2).
The error is linked to the field with aria-invalid and announced when it appears (SC 3.3.1, 4.1.3).
The drag state is not conveyed by colour alone: the text changes to "Drop to upload" (SC 1.4.1).

keyboard.action: Move to the Upload button
Open the system file chooser
Remove or replace the chosen file

components.name: Connector picker
components.summary: Search and connect outside services. Each row says what connecting lets the product do, and a dialog explains the access before anything is shared.
structure: Row (logo, name, what it lets the product do, Connect, Reconnect or Manage)
Connect dialog (access in plain words, who it is shared with, OAuth or API key, Cancel)

whenToUse.t: Connecting several outside services, from onboarding or from Settings.
Showing what is connected and what needs attention in one place.

whenNotToUse.t: Setting what an agent may do with a tool. Use Agent permissions (agent-permissions).
Reviewing one tool in depth. Use the detail card in Connected tools (connected-tools).

guidelines.t: Add search with the count of services, and put Connected first.
Say what connecting lets the product do, in plain words, before connecting: "Read and send email".
Say who the connection is shared with, for example "Only you" or "Everyone in TwoUX".
OAuth opens the provider in a new window. Say so on the button ("Continue to Slack") and bring people back with a status message.
Test an API key before saving it, store it encrypted and never show it again. Say all three beside the field.
When a connection expires, show Needs attention with the reason and a Reconnect button, never colour alone.
Disconnecting lives in Settings and asks what stops working before it does.

content.t: "Read your calendar to find free times. Cannot change events."
"Slack needs you to sign in again. Reconnect to resume the daily summary."

accessibility.t: Rows are a list under group headings; the group names are real headings (SC 1.3.1).
Buttons repeat the service name for assistive technology: "Connect Slack" (SC 2.4.6, 4.1.2).
The dialog traps focus, returns it to the button and announces success with role="status" (APG dialog, SC 4.1.3).
Status is carried by words (Connected, Needs attention) as well as colour (SC 1.4.1).

keyboard.action: Move through the search, then each row's button
Connect, Reconnect or Manage
Close the dialog without connecting

components.name: Code block
components.summary: Shows code, commands, IDs or log output exactly as written, so people can read and copy it. Inline Code marks a token inside a sentence.
structure: Actions: copy button, more if needed

whenToUse.t: To let people copy a command, token, API key name or snippet exactly.
To show a change as a diff, with added and removed lines.
To show tool or agent output, such as a run log, using the small size.
Inline Code for a prop, token or file name inside a sentence: `bg-surface`, `jobs.json`.

whenNotToUse.t: When people need to edit the text. Use a Text input or the Prompt editor.
For ordinary values in a table, such as an ID column. Use the mono table cell.
Inline Code across several lines. Use a code block.

guidelines.t: Long single-line commands scroll sideways rather than wrapping, so they stay copyable as one line. Use wrap for prose-like output.
Past about nine lines, cap the height and offer Show more in the footer.
Without a header, the copy button floats top right and appears on hover or focus, and always on touch screens.
Line numbers are optional, never copied and hidden from screen readers.
Use the destructive variant for errors and failed output.
Light border, grey fill: the block is read, not raised, so it takes no shadow.

content.t: Label the header with the file name or what the code is: “twoux.css”, “Install”, “Run log”.
Show code exactly as it should be typed. No ellipses inside commands.

accessibility.t: The scrolling area is focusable (tabindex 0) so keyboard users can scroll it.
Added and removed lines show + and − as well as colour.
Copying announces “Copied” through a status message without moving focus; focus stays on the button.
Wrapping is available so long output does not force two-dimensional scrolling at 320px.
Code text keeps 4.5:1 on the grey fill; line numbers use ink-3 (5.4:1 on surface-2).

keyboard.action: Focus the code area, then the copy button
Scroll the code area when it has focus
Copy, when the copy button has focus

components.name: Card
components.summary: A white container that groups one object or one task, such as a settings section, a sign-in form or a summary, with an optional header, actions and footer.
structure: Container: white, light edge, 6px corners, resting shadow
Action (optional): one button or menu, top right
Footer (optional): actions on the right, or a tinted band with one secondary line

whenToUse.t: To group the fields and actions of one settings section or one form, so it reads as one unit.
To show one summary of an object, such as a listing's status and owner, on a page that holds several.

whenNotToUse.t: For rows of a list or table. Use the List table; cards break scanning and comparison across rows.
Inside another card. Use a Separator or a heading to divide the content instead.
To make text stand out. Use a Banner for a condition, or plain hierarchy.

guidelines.t: One card is one object or one task. If the content splits into two jobs, use two cards.
Keep the header short: a title, an optional one-line description, and at most one action on the right.
Put primary actions in the footer, right-aligned, with the main action last.
Use the footer band for a single secondary line, such as “Already have an account? Sign in”.
Cards on a white page keep their edge; cards on the grey app background can drop the shadow but keep the edge.

content.t: Title in sentence case naming the object or task: “Notifications”, “Salary bands”.
The description says what the section controls, not how to use the card.

accessibility.t: When a card holds a section, give the title a real heading element at the right level, so it appears in the heading list.
Do not make the whole card clickable when it contains other controls; link the title instead, so each target has one purpose.
The card edge is decorative; the content does not rely on it to be understood.

keyboard.action: Moves through the card's own controls in reading order; the card itself is not a stop

components.name: Separator
components.summary: A thin line that divides groups of content or menu items. With a label, it separates two ways of doing the same thing, such as “or”.
structure: Label (optional): short word centred on the line, on the surface colour

whenToUse.t: To divide groups inside a card, panel or menu when spacing alone is not enough.
With a label, between two routes to the same result: “or” between sign in with Google and the email form.

whenNotToUse.t: Between every row or field. Use spacing; lines everywhere add noise.
To separate sections of a page. Use headings and space.

guidelines.t: Prefer space first. Add a line only where groups would otherwise run together.
Keep the label to one or two words in lower case: “or”, “or continue with”.
Lines run the full width of their container, or align with the content inset in menus.

content.t: Label in lower case with no full stop: “or”.

accessibility.t: A purely visual line is decorative, so screen readers skip it. Mark it as a separator only when it divides a menu or a toolbar.
The label is real text, so it is read in order between the two groups.

keyboard.action: Not focusable

components.name: Timestamp
components.summary: One component for every date and time in the product: relative or absolute display, the exact value on hover and focus, and an optional "by" source.
structure: Optional label, when not given by a column header or key: "Last edited"
Value: relative ("3 hours ago") or absolute ("6 November 2026, 14:32 GMT")
Optional source: "by Priya Shah", linked to the profile, with "via Assistant" when applied from a proposal
Tooltip with the absolute value on hover and focus

whenToUse.t: Every time a date or time appears: table columns, side panel details, activity, Inbox items, "Last updated" after a refresh.
format="relative" for recent past events in lists; format="absolute" for details and deadlines; format="iso" for code and exports.
source="Priya Shah" when it matters who made the change, such as Last edited on a listing.

whenNotToUse.t: For date entry. Use a date input.
For durations, such as "Time to hire: 18 days"; that is a number with a unit, not a timestamp.
For a date with no time that is a property of the record, such as a start date. Show it as an absolute date.

guidelines.t: Renders a <time> element with the ISO 8601 value in datetime.
Relative values tick over once a minute; they never animate or announce.
Time zone is the viewer's own and is always shown on absolute values.
In compact table cells, `short` shows "3h ago" or "20 Nov"; the tooltip and accessible name keep the full form.
Future deadlines use absolute dates, optionally followed by relative time in muted text.
Give deadlines, start dates and due dates as a date with no time (2026-12-07). They show as 7 December 2026, with no time or zone, and fall on the same day in every time zone.

content.t: Relative: "Just now", "5 minutes ago", "3 hours ago", "2 days ago", "In 3 days".
Absolute: day, month in full, year, 24-hour time, zone: "6 November 2026, 14:32 GMT".
Source: "Edited 6 hours ago by Priya Shah".

accessibility.t: The accessible description carries the absolute value, so screen reader users don't need the tooltip.
The tooltip appears on focus of the cell or link that contains the timestamp, without adding a separate tab stop.
Never put a ticking relative time in a live region.

keyboard.keys: Tab or arrows (to the containing cell or link)
keyboard.action: Show the absolute time tooltip
Hide the tooltip
Move to the person's profile link

components.name: Provider logo
components.summary: The official mark of a service people sign in with or connect, shown unaltered on a white tile beside the service's name.
structure: Tile (white in both themes, hairline border)

whenToUse.t: Identifying a service someone signs in with, such as Google or Microsoft.
Identifying a service someone connects, such as Slack or Google Drive, in a list or a connection dialog.

whenNotToUse.t: Marking a competitor or a product we studied as a reference. Those get a text name only.
Decoration, avatars or a stand-in for our own brand. Use Avatar (avatar) for people and the product mark for us.
Logos of services that are not connectable. A mark implies the connection exists.

guidelines.t: Use the official mark only for third-party services people sign in with or connect. Never for competitors or reference products.
Show the mark unaltered: no recolouring, no cropping, no effects, no new background shapes.
Put the mark beside the service's name. When it stands alone, give it a label so the service is still named.
Keep the tile white in light and dark themes so dark marks, such as GitHub and Notion, stay visible.
To add a provider, add a line to the list in scripts/provider-logos.mjs and run node scripts/provider-logos.mjs. Check the brand's own page for permitted use first.
The icon sources are licensed for reuse: Iconify's logos set is CC0, vscode-icons and thesvg-color are MIT. Trademarks stay with their owners, so show a mark only to identify that service.

content.t: "Continue with Google" and "Connect Slack": the name is always in words, never only in the mark.
When alone, label it with the service name only, for example "Google Drive".

accessibility.t: Beside a visible name the mark is decorative and hidden from assistive technology. Alone, it has role="img" and an aria-label with the service name (SC 1.1.1).
The tile keeps the mark's edges distinct from either theme (SC 1.4.11).

keyboard.action: Not focusable. The button or row that contains it is the focus stop.
